Looking at this problem, I need to determine which lines on a smooth quadric surface $Q \subset \mathbb{P}^3$ satisfy the condition that some plane $P$ has $2l \subseteq P \cap Q$ (i.e., $l$ appears as a double line in the plane section).

## Setting Up the Geometry

A smooth quadric $Q \cong \mathbb{P}^1 \times \mathbb{P}^1$ in $\mathbb{P}^3$ contains exactly two rulings of lines. Using coordinates with $Q: x_0 x_3 - x_1 x_2 = 0$:

- **Ruling 1:** For each $[u:v] \in \mathbb{P}^1$, the line is $\{x_0 v - x_1 u = 0,\; x_2 v - x_3 u = 0\}$
- **Ruling 2:** For each $[s:t] \in \mathbb{P}^1$, the line is $\{x_0 t - x_2 s = 0,\; x_1 t - x_3 s = 0\}$

The Fano variety is $F(Q) \cong \mathbb{P}^1 \sqcup \mathbb{P}^1$.

## Analyzing the Condition $2l \subseteq P \cap Q$

For $P \cap Q$ to contain $2l$, the plane $P$ must be **tangent to $Q$ at every point of $l$** (so that the degree-2 plane section has a double-line component).

The tangent plane to $Q$ at a point $[a:b:c:d]$ is:
$$dX_0 - cX_1 - bX_2 + aX_3 = 0$$

The **Gauss map** $Q \xrightarrow{\sim} Q^\vee$ (sending each point to its tangent plane) is an **isomorphism** for a smooth quadric. This means the tangent plane at $p$ equals the tangent plane at $q$ **if and only if** $p = q$.

Since a line $l$ contains infinitely many points, there is **no single plane** that can serve as the tangent plane at every point of $l$.

## Direct Coordinate Verification

Taking $l = \{x_1 = 0,\, x_3 = 0\}$ (a Ruling 1 line), any plane $P$ containing $l$ must have equation $x_1 - \lambda x_3 = 0$. Substituting into $Q$:

$$x_0 x_3 - \lambda x_3 x_2 = x_3(x_0 - \lambda x_2) = 0$$

This factors as:
$$P \cap Q = \underbrace{\{x_3 = 0,\; x_1 = 0\}}_{= \, l} \;\;\cup\;\; \underbrace{\{x_0 = \lambda x_2,\; x_1 = \lambda x_3\}}_{= \, l' \text{ (Ruling 2 line)}}$$

The two lines are **distinct** and meet transversely at exactly one point $[\lambda:0:1:0]$. The intersection is **reduced** everywhere—no double-line component ever appears.

## Conclusion

For a smooth quadric surface, the condition $2l \subseteq P \cap Q$ is **never satisfied** by any line $l$ on $Q$ and any plane $P$. Therefore:

$$F_{osc} = \emptyset$$

The degree of the empty zero cycle is:

$$\boxed{0}$$
